NATIONALAERONAUTICSAND SPACE ADMINISTRATION

 CHARTEROF THE

 NASA ADVISORYCOUNCIL

1. Official Designation: NASA Advisory Council e'Council").

2. Authority: Having determinedthat it is in the public interest in connection with the
performanceof Agency duties under the law, and withthe concurrence of the General Services
Administration,the NASA Administratorhereby renews the Council's charter, pursuant to the
Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA), as amended, 5 U.S.C., App.

3. Objectives and Scope of Activities: The Council shall draw on the expertise of its members
and other sources to provide advice and make recommendationsto the NASA Administratoron
Agency programs, policies, plans, financial controls, and other matters pertinent to the Agency's
responsibilities. The Council shall also encourage and review proposed committee
recommendationsfor Associate Administrators.

4. Descriptionof Duties: The Council shall fimctioilsolely as an advisory body and comply
with the provisions of FACA. The Council shall be supported by committees, subcommittees,
and task forces as needed, to cover the breadth and depth of scope as determinedby the NASA
Administrator.

5. Official to Whom the CommitteeReports: The Council reports to the NASA
Administrator. The committeesreport to the Council.

6. Support: The Office of Internationaland Interagency Relations will provide staff support
and operatingfunds for the Council. The Mission Directorates and/or Mission Support Offices
shall provide staff support and operating funds for the respective committees,subcommittees,
and task forces which report to the Council.

7. EstimatedAnnual Operating Costs and Staff Years: The estimated annual operating cost
for the Council, its committees, subcommittees,and task forces totals approximately$850,000,
including three work-years for staff support.

8. DesignatedFederal Officer: The Executive Director of the Council shall be appointedby
the NASA Administratorand shall serve as the Designated Federal Officer (DFO). The DFO
will be either a full-time or a perm.anentpart-time employee who will: call, attend, and adjourn
committee meetings; approve agendas; maintain required records on costs and membership;
ensure efficient operations; maintain records for availability to the public; and provide copies of
Council reports to the NASA Committee Management Officer for forwardingto the Library of
Congress. The DFO shall also work closely with the NASA Office of General Counsel (OGC)
to ensure that all potential members (i.e., nominees) for the Council, committees,subcommittees,
and task forces complete the mandatory Office of Government Ethics financial disclosurereports
and receive full ethics vetting and clearance by OGC prior to formal appointmentby NASA. In
 2

addition, the DFO shall ensure that all appointed members of the Council. committees,
subcommittees, and task forces shall file the mandatory financial disclosure reports (annual and
otherwise) and shall receive the mandatory annual ethics training by OGC. The DFO shall refer
any issues that may arise relating •to potential conflicts of interest to OGC for resolution.

9. EstimatedNumber and Frequency of Meetings: The Council shall meet approximately
three times a year or as required by the NASA Administrator. Meetings shall be open to the
public unless it is determined that the meeting, or a portion of the meeting, will be closed in
accordance with the Government in the Sunshine Act.

10. Duration: The Council is envisioned to be a continuing entity with charter renewals.

11. Termination: As noted in Paragraph 15, the Council shall terminate two years from the
date of the filing of the original charter unless renewed or terminated earlier by the NASA
Administrator. ·

12. Membershipand Designation:

 1. The Council shall consist of members to be appointed by the NASA Administrator ( or
 designee). The Administrator shall ensure a balanced representation in terms of the
 points of view represented and the functions to be performed. Diversity shall be
 considered as well.

 2. The Council shall consist of approximately 10-20 members. who will serve as Special
 Government Employees for a two-year term, renewable at the discretion of the NASA
 Administrator, except the Chairof the Regulatory .and Policy Committee will serve on the
 Council as a Representative or Special Government Employee as determined by the ·
 NASA Administrator, for a two-year renewable term. Special Government Employees
 serve as individual subject matter experts. and Representatives serve to represent the
 interests of their specific sectors. All Council members serve at the pleasure of the
 Adniinistrator.

 3. The NASA Administrator shall designate the Chair of the Council.

 4. The Council shall be comprised of the Chair, the committee chairs, and at-large members,
 as appropriate, at the discretion of the NASA Administrator.

 5. The chairs of the National Research Council's Space Studies Board (SSB) and the
 Aeronautics and Space Engineering Board (ASEB) shall be ex officio, nonvoting
 members of the Council.

13. Committees,Subcommittees,and Task Forces:

 1. The NASA Administrator shall establish the following Council committees,
 subcommittees, and task forces:
 3

 • AeronauticsCommittee.
 • HumanExplorationand OperationsCommittee.
 • Regulatoryand Policy Committee.
 • ScienceCommittee.
 • Technology,Innovation, and EngineeringCommittee.
 • Ad Hoc Task Force on Science,Technology,Engineering,and Mathematics
 (STEM)Education.

2. Councilcommittees,subcommittees,and task forces may be established or discontinued
 at the discretionof the NASA Administrator. No formal amendment(s)to this charter
 will be requiredto effect such change(s).

3. The NASA Administrator,in consultationwith the Council Chair, may establish
 committeesunder the Council, as necessary. The tenns of reference for committeesshall
 be subjectto the approval of the Administrator. Council committees shall consist of
 membersto be appointedby the Administrator(or designee). Council committeesshall
 be comprisedof 5-15 members, includingthe chair, and will be chaired by a Council
 member. Each committeeshall deliberatethe recommendationsthat arise from the
 committeeor are received from their subcommittees,if any. In the latter case, the
 committeemay endorse subcommitteerecommendationsand forward them to the
 Councilfor deliberations,or the committeemay provide comments_orsuggestionsback
 to the subcommittee.

4. The Council shall deliberate the recommendationsof the committeesand any task forces
 that may report directly to the Council. Toe Councilmay forward a recommendationto
 the NASA Administratorfor Agency considerationor return it to the committeewith
 commentspertaining to its disposition,includingrequests for revision and resubmission,
 and confirmationof its recommendedtransmissionto the appropriateAssociate
 Administratorfor consideration. In general, Council recommendationsto the
 Administratorpertain to strategic, crosscutting,Agency-wide,programmatic,and policy
 topics. In general, committee recommendationsapprovedby the Councilfor the
 committeesto transmit to AssociateAdministratorspertain to missions,programs,
 projects,and research topics. All recommendationsforwardedto the Administratoror to
 an AssociateAdministratorshall be tracked by the respectiveCouncilExecutiveDirector
 or CommitteeExecutive Secretary,as appropriate. An Agency formal written response
 to each recommendationsubmittedto the Administratorshall be providedto the Council.
 Similarly,a formal written responseto each recommendationsubmittedto an Associate
 Administratorshall be provided to the appropriatecommittee. A·copy of each response
 by a NASA Associate Administratorshall be .provided by the relevant Committee
 ExecutiveSecretaryto the Council ExecutiveDirector,to ensure full compliancewith
 FACA and Federal record.keepingrequirements. No Council committeeshall be
 independentlychartered under FACA.

5. The NASA Administrator,in consultationwith the Council Chair, may establish
 subcommitteesunder the Council committees,as necessary~The terms of referencefor
 subcommitteesshall be subject to the approval of the Administrator. A memberof the
 subcommittee'sparent committeeshall chair the subcommittee. The membersof
 subcommitteesshall be appointedby the respectiveAssociateAdministratorfollowing
 4

 consultation with the Administrator. The subcommittees shall report to their respective
 committee(s).

 6. The NASA Administrator, in consultation with the Council Chair, may establish
 temporary ad hoc task forces under the Council or under specific Council committees, as
 necessary. The terms of reference for task forces shall be subject to the approval of the
 Administrator. Task force chairs and members shall be appointed by the Administrator
 (or designee).

 7. To ensure close coordination and transparency, and avoid duplication of effort, the chairs
 of the following other NASA-chartered Federal advisory committees shall also serve as a
 member of the respective Cowicil committee:

 • Astrophysics Advisory Committee (Science Committee)
 • Earth Science Advisory Committee (Science Committee)
 • HeliophysicsAdvisory Committee (Science Committee)
 • Planetary Science Advisory Committee (Science Committee)
 • HumflllExploration and Operations Research Advisory Committee (Human
 Exploration and Operations Committee)

14. Reeordkeeping: The records of the Council, its committees, subcommittees, and task
forces shall be handled in accordance with the General Records Schedule 6.2, or other approved
Agency records disposition schedule. These records shall be available for public inspection and
copying, subject to the Freedom oflnfonnation Act, 5 U.S.C. 552.

15. Filing Date: This charter shall become effective upon the filing of this charter with the
appropriate U.S. Senate and House of Representatives oversight committees. It shall terminate
two yea.rsfrom the date of filing of this charter unless renewed or terminated earlier by the
NASA Administrator.
